original.target_description: Bateson (2012), published article, crime victimization and political participation across multiple regional surveys and nine dependent variables; individual target test unspecified.

replication.target_description: Identified by the supplied primary replication report: LAPOP/AmericasBarometer 2010 community action (frequency of solving problems in community/neighborhood), regressed on past-year crime victimization with sex, age, age squared, socioeconomic status, education, urbanization and country fixed effects; robust SE clustered by municipality.

n.sample_role: participants included in replication; report does not explicitly distinguish regression complete cases from overall replication sample

reported_success.quote: Thus, this replication of the claim was successful according to the SCORE criteria.

notes:
Input study identifiers, description and locators are empty. Target identified independently from supplied primary replication report. Report title and project ID match supplied reference; author header lists Andrew Tyner and Anna Szabelska. Replication report gives 38020 included participants but does not explicitly identify regression complete cases or exclusions; n is retained as a named replication sample with confidence false, not asserted analytic n. Requested replication es_type ser_method is not a printed metric; printed coefficient extracted without conversion. Original DOI title verified. DOI landing page provided abstract/access only; Unpaywall and OpenAlex returned no OA location. Vanderbilt candidate PDF contained only a cover and opening page; rejected as incomplete. Author research page offered DOI link only. No original statistic inferred from replication or incomplete original. Original acquisition miss recorded in text cache.
Source follow-up: Original primary article located and read (published pp. 570–587). No study identifier, neutral effect description, outcome, region, model or source locator is supplied. Table 4 alone contains many distinct region-by-outcome coefficients. Cannot identify the intended original test, analytic sample, effect size or same-test p without guessing. The three assigned rows provide indistinguishable original-side target information. Unassigned replication side is intentionally unavailable. Canonical primary TXT was read; target PDF pages were visually checked where locators were supplied. No statistics were inferred from row ordering.
